summary: custom roles_v2 claim not mapped to RBAC, customer admins appear read-only in private deployment
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that several users who should have tenant-admin privileges in their private deployment are only seeing read-only views in the Redwood Console. This started after a recent IdP configuration change (rolled by the customer) where their IdP began emitting a new claim named "roles_v2" as an array of objects instead of the legacy "roles" string list.

Impact:
- Multiple DataSentry users cannot perform admin actions (create API keys, manage billing visibility, manage dedicated pools) despite being marked as admins in the IdP.
- Customer-facing admin workflows are blocked for a small group (~6 users) in prod us-west-2.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC) for DataSentry Inc.
- Console version: 3.4.2
- Identity proxy version: 2.8.1

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Login with affected user via customer IdP through private Console URL (https://console.datasentry.example).
2) Observe Console: top-right shows expected tenant and username.
3) Attempt to access Organization -> Admin settings -> Manage API keys -> button is disabled/hidden.
4) Call Admins API (GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/members) with bearer token from affected user; response shows role: member.

Expected behavior:
- Users with admin roles emitted by IdP should be mapped to tenant-admin role in Redwood RBAC and have full admin capabilities.

Actual behavior:
- The identity proxy ignores "roles_v2" claim; downstream role-mapping logic only reads "roles". As a result, users are treated as non-admins.

Logs / traces included by customer (redacted):
- Identity proxy authn debug: "claim roles missing; fallback to empty role list"
- Customer SAML response excerpt (redacted): "roles_v2": [{"name":"tenant-admin","scope":"org:12345"}, {"name":"billing-admin","scope":"org:12345"}]

Additional notes:
- Customer confirmed they intentionally switched to a richer claim structure for future-proofing.
- This began on 2026-03-09 after IdP config change.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Identity proxy only deserializes 'roles' as []string; structured arrays under 'roles_v2' are ignored by claim normalizer.
Reproduction: Created test IdP response with roles_v2 as array of objects: identity-proxy returned no roles to RBAC pipeline; console served 'member' role.
Observed metrics: authz decision logs in prod show 'role_count=0' for affected tokens between 2026-03-09T14:12 and 2026-03-09T14:30 UTC.
Cause: Schema mismatch; customer changed to object-based role claim without coordinating mapping change in identity-proxy config. No prior validation blocked ingest of non-legacy claim names.
Risk assessment: Low risk to platform but high product impact for this customer (admin tasks blocked). Other private deployments could have similar custom claims.
Workaround validated: IdP transformation (copy roles_v2[*].name -> roles[]) restores expected behavior immediately.

Planned fix: Add configurable claim mappers to identity-proxy to support nested arrays and custom claim names; include a default compatibility layer that will map detected roles_v2 -> roles for a 2-release window.
resolution_notes: Workaround: Customer applied an IdP transformation to copy roles_v2[*].name into legacy roles[] claim; verified by Support that admin privileges restored for affected users. Engineering created PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/478 to add configurable claim mappers and a compatibility heuristic for common 'roles_v2' structures. Rollout plan: stage patch in canary private deployments (week of 2026-03-15), then push to stable pipeline 2026-03-22. Post-deploy: notify customers with custom claims and recommend they remove temporary IdP transformation after the compatibility window. Follow-ups: update private-deploy quickstart docs with claim mapping guidance and add an automated validation check during onboarding to detect non-standard role claim shapes.
public_resolution_summary: Identified that DataSentry's IdP emits admin roles in a nested 'roles_v2' claim which our identity proxy did not map to RBAC. Customer applied a temporary IdP transformation to populate the legacy 'roles' claim; Engineering will add configurable claim mappers and a temporary compatibility layer so structured role claims are supported without customer transformations.
